The '''2012–13''' season of the '''[[Belgian Pro League]]''' (also known as ''[[Jupiler]] Pro League'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 110th season of top-tier football in [[Belgium]]. It started on 28 July 2012 with the first match of the regular season between [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] and defending champions [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]],<ref name=schedule>{{cite news |title=Kortrijk-Anderlecht opens new competition |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1327755|publisher=sporza.be |date=2012-06-11|language=nl}}</ref> and ended on 26 May 2013, which was the return leg of the European playoff.

During the regular season, [[Club Brugge K.V.|Club Brugge]] took the early lead but then started struggling, eventually leading to the sacking of head coach [[Georges Leekens]] when they dropped out of the top 6 in November. Anderlecht and overachievers [[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]] took over the top two positions and comfortably held these until the playoffs.

The title playoffs started with Anderlecht on 34 points and Zulte Waregem just behind them on 32. Due to the division of the points by two, they held a smaller lead over [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]] (28 points), Club Brugge (27), [[K.S.C. Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen|Lokeren]] (26) and [[Standard Liège|Standard]] (25). To the surprise of many, Zulte Waregem took the lead about halfway through the playoffs and with Anderlecht not performing well and suffering a penalty kick trauma (missing no less than 10 penalty kicks over the course of the season and going out on penalties to Genk in the [[2012–13 Belgian Cup|Belgian Cup]]), both Genk, Club Brugge and Standard Liège rapidly close the gap. Anderlecht managed to overtake Zulte Waregem again and went into the final match on 19 May 2013, at home against Zulte Waregem, with a two-point lead. Anderlecht equalized after going down 0-1 and under pressure managed to hold on, even though losing [[Cheikhou Kouyaté]] due to a red card. With that, Anderlecht won its 32nd title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/20130519/anderlecht-wins-belgian-league-title.ap/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203094810/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/20130519/anderlecht-wins-belgian-league-title.ap/|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 February 2014|title= Anderlecht wins Belgian league title|date=19 May 2013|work=Sports Illustrated|access-date=25 July 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/0257-0def299b8f1a-6a0bbc9b072e-1000--anderlecht-hold-off-zulte-waregem-to-seal-title/|title= Anderlecht hold off Zulte Waregem to seal title|date=19 May 2013|publisher=UEFA|access-date=25 July 2013 }}</ref>
The draw allowed Zulte Waregem to remain just in front of Club Brugge, thereby gaining access to the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. Club Brugge and Genk qualified for the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]], due to finishing 3rd and winning the Cup respectively.

The Europa League playoff groups were won by [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]] and [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven]], with Gent easily beating OH Leuven for the overall win. Gent had played a disappointing season, initially aiming for the top 6 but eventually finishing 12th. By winning the Europa League playoff, they won the right to play against [[Standard Liège]] for the final Europa League ticket. Gent won the first match 1-0 but lost the return 7–0, allowing Standard to take the last European ticket.

In the bottom end of the table, [[Cercle Brugge KSV|Cercle Brugge]] faced a miserable season after finishing 7th the previous season, as now only three wins and five draws out of thirty matches caused them to end in last place. [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse]] narrowly held of [[Beerschot A.C.|Beerschot]], causing Cercle Brugge and Beerschot to play the relegation playoff. Beerschot initially extended their lead, but Cercle Brugge came back and on 20 April 2013, a 2–1 win by Cercle caused Beerschot to be relegated. Beerschot had been playing in the top division since [[1989–90 Belgian First Division|1989–90]], initially as Germinal Ekeren, then as Germinal Beerschot. A few days after the relegation it was announced that Beerschot was in severe financial trouble and was not given a license for professional football. On 21 May, Beerschot was officially declared bankrupt and dissolved as a whole. Cercle Brugge on the other hand, had to play the [[Belgian Second Division final rounds 2011–20#2013|Belgian Second Division final round]] with second division teams [[Royal Mouscron-Péruwelz|Mouscron-Péruwelz]], [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]] and [[White Star Woluwe F.C.|WS Woluwe]]. On 23 May 2013, Cercle Brugge became the first team succeeding in avoiding relegation after playing the relegation playoff, since the installation of the playoffs system in [[2009–10 Belgian Pro League|2009–10]].

==Teams==
Following the [[2011–12 Belgian Pro League]], [[Sint-Truidense V.V.|Sint-Truiden]] were relegated to the [[2012–13 Belgian Second Division]] after losing their [[2011–12 Belgian Pro League#Relegation Playoff|relegation playoff series]] against [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]], ending a three-season tenure in the league. Sint-Truiden were replaced by [[2011–12 Belgian Second Division|2011–12 Second Division]] champions [[R. Charleroi S.C.|Charleroi]], who made their immediate comeback to the highest Belgian football league. In the [[Belgian Second Division final rounds 2011–20#2012|2012 Belgian Second Division final round]], [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]] faced Second Division teams [[K. A. S. Eupen|Eupen]], [[K. V. Oostende|Oostende]] and [[Waasland-Beveren]]. On 17 May 2012, Westerlo were relegated after a 0–0 draw away to Oostende. Also in Oostende, Waasland-Beveren secured the promotion one week later after a 1–1 draw.

===Positions by round===
Note: The classification was made after the weekend (or midweek) of each matchday, so postponed matches were only processed at the time they were played to represent the ''real'' evolution in standings.

The following matches were postponed during the season:
* Matchday 23: on 20 January both the match between leaders Anderlecht and second placed Zulte Waregem and the [[Bruges derby]] between Club Brugge and Cercle Brugge were postponed due to intensive snowing. They have been rescheduled to be played end of February between matchdays 28 and 29.<ref name=ppmd23>{{cite news |title=Postponed matches to be played end of February|url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1530136
|publisher=sporza.be |language=nl |date=2013-01-20}}</ref>
* Matchday 24: also due to snow, the match between Charleroi and Cercle Brugge was postponed on 26 January. The match was played on 20 February, between matchdays 27 and 28.<ref name=ppmd24>{{cite news |title=Charleroi-Cercle Brugge cancelled due to severe weather conditions |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1533997
|publisher=sporza.be |language=nl |date=2013-01-26}}</ref>
* Matchday 28: yet again it was snow that prevented a match to be played. The fixture between Charleroi and Zulte Waregem was postponed on 24 February and rescheduled to 3 March, between matchdays 28 and 29.<ref name=ppmd28>{{cite news |title=Charleroi-Zulte Waregem cancelled |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1554757
|publisher=sporza.be |language=nl |date=2013-02-24}}</ref>

==Championship playoff==
The points obtained during the regular season were halved (and rounded up) before the start of the playoff. As a result, the teams started with the following points before the playoff: Anderlecht 34 points, Zulte Waregem 32, Genk 28, Club Brugge 27, Lokeren 26 and Standard 25. In the event of ties at the end of the playoffs, the half point will be deducted if it was added. Anderlecht, Genk, Lokeren and Zulte Waregem received this type of bonus due to rounding and will thus always be ranked below Club Brugge and Standard in the event of ties.

==Relegation playoff==
Beerschot and Cercle Brugge, the teams finishing in the last two positions, faced each other in the relegation playoff. Beerschot initially extended their three-point bonus to a six-point lead, but thereafter Cercle Brugge won three matches in a row. This caused Beerschot to be relegated to the [[Belgian Second Division|Second Division]] on 20 April 2013 after playing in the first division since 1989 (as ''Germinal Ekeren'' until 1999 and as ''Germinal Beerschot'' from 1999 until 2011). One month later however, it was announced that Beerschot had gone bankrupt and dissolved.

Cercle Brugge was forced to play the second division playoff with three [[Belgian Second Division]] teams, which they won to avoid relegation. It was the first time a team from the Pro League succeeded in surviving the Second Division Final Round since the installment of the Belgian Pro League playoffs.<!--
adjust_points parameter denotes starting points for the team ending in 15th position during the regular season
